elements.text: Signing MUST reuse the shipped SealSet (glp_crdtmsg/sig/Seals.cs) and Ed25519Signer (Olamnit.Shared/Yngenios/Seal/, BouncyCastle RFC-8032). A bespoke chained-signature implementation is FORBIDDEN: gavri's independent 3-critic panel found the proposed chain was a weaker re-implementation of shipped, CI-tested infrastructure. Rationale: reusing a shipped realization beats a new peer implementation (standing layering law).

A SOLE verifier/persister can truncate or roll back the chain undetected. Therefore: all-node CO-SIGNED witness checkpoints plus a monotonic per-run sequence, with run_id, position and roster BOUND INTO THE SIGNED BODY. Unbound fields are forgeable by replay across runs/positions. This checkpoint surface is also the independent record the E-B corroborator reads (see M-12).

A rigid ring HALTS on a dead node; the real DV mesh REROUTES. The soak MUST ride the REAL ynet DV mesh (@mesh / MeshNodeRuntime, QUIC/WS + crdtmsg envelopes) — the 'two triangles' topology — and NEVER freestanding raw links. Operator hard constraint, independently confirmed by gavri's panel. Consequence: the name 'ring' denotes the logical relay order, NOT a pinned physical path.

Fail semantics are SPLIT and must not be conflated: a BAD SIGNATURE (integrity failure) HALTS the run and is recorded; a LINK DROP (liveness failure) REROUTES via DV and is COUNTED, not fatal. Reuse the shipped MeshSendOutcome closed value set rather than inventing outcomes.

fsync-per-cycle caps throughput at ~50 cycles/s => 1M cycles = 5-12 h. FSYNC BINDS THE BUDGET, NOT BLE — this refutes the assumption that radio latency dominates. Mitigations: batch B cycles under a group commit + Merkle-root chaining; CRC-framed group-commit resume; cache the expanded Ed25519 key. Crypto is NOT the bottleneck (verified in gavri's impl-plan: ~72 MB, minutes at group-commit).

An EPHEMERAL per-launch amulet key is the exact trap that broke the KV bench pins: identities churn across restarts and pinned vectors stop verifying. The relay identity key MUST be stable across restarts (the EndorserKey.cs pattern: derive from a created-once host secret under domain separation).

Identity is by AddressBook/@name, NEVER raw IP: olamnit is multi-homed (.129/.136/.143) and is ONE identity. CORRECTION folded from gavri's critic: AddressBook.Resolve DOES NOT EXIST — the real API is PrefixRouteTable.TryResolve(ushort). Any design or claim citing AddressBook.Resolve is built on a non-existent symbol and must be rejected.

The DV mesh path is CLEARTEXT today — there is no secure wrap on it. Folded from gavri's critic. Any claim that the soak demonstrates confidentiality, or that relay bodies are protected in transit, is FALSE. State the gap; do not design around it silently and do not let the evidence report imply protection that does not exist.

The real adapter risk is FAULT-SEMANTICS (a transient fault escalating into a permanent-down storm), NOT the type split. Folded from gavri's critic, which corrected the original risk attribution. Investigate transient-vs-permanent classification and storm damping; do not spend the budget on the type split.

RULED (E-A, lead): merge=max for the replicated wallet is REJECTED as a category error. The ledger is a conservation DAG of tokens (CoinDag/CoinToken/MicroCoin) with five commutative ops (mint/charge/split/merge/aging) admitted against conservation, no-negative and exactly-once (DAG consumed-flags), WAL as sole source-of-record. There is NO SCALAR BALANCE TO MAX — balance is PROJECTED from unconsumed tokens. Convergence comes from commutativity + dot idempotence, not a lattice max. Suspected origin of the error: 'merge' is ALREADY an op name (token merge) — conflating token-merge with replica-merge. Do not re-import this confusion into the design.

RULED (E-A, lead): the E-A work is EXACTLY the pre-existing in-code follow-up OE-4, and kill-one is NOT descoped. The danger is real but the mechanism is specific: folding peer ops bypasses the admission path where conservation/no-negative/exactly-once are enforced, so peer ops are not re-validated before projecting. Scope: (1) MergeFrom and rehydration must re-validate (admission + witness-cert) BEFORE projecting; (2) Replay must accept a committed SpendBody. This is NOT a new CRDT and NOT a lattice. Layer: L0/L1 (contract + common core), never per-platform. NOTE FOR THE CRITIC: this ruling rests on the lead's own reading; slice-coin-ledger-merge investigates the same surface BLIND. If the blind Builder's finding contradicts this element, the Builder's evidence wins and this element must be re-opened.

RULED (E-B, lead): relay-transmit claims are AUTO-ENDORSABLE, conditional on the corroborator being the SUCCESSOR'S ACK, never the claimant's own record. Grounds: the shipped independence rule is a single string inequality (endorser key != claimant wallet) that passes BY CONSTRUCTION under domain separation, so it is a backstop and NOT the guarantee; the load-bearing independence is the EVIDENCE. Project precedent decides it — an existing work class is pinned fail-closed MANUAL with the recorded reason that no independent corroboration source exists for it, establishing that auto-endorsability is EARNED by an independent corroborator, never by holding a distinct key. The successor's Ed25519 ack (bound run_id/position/roster per M-02) is unforgeable by the claimant and is therefore STRONGER evidence than the shipped corroborators, which re-read records the claimant's own host wrote. Consequence: the ack-gate is not merely fraud prevention on the earning side — the ack is what MANUFACTURES the independent evidence.

MANDATORY CAVEAT on M-12 — the evidence report MUST NOT overclaim it. The relay corroborator gives independence against a FORGING adversary, NOT against a FULLY BYZANTINE HOST: a byzantine node controlling its own durable store could insert an endorsement row directly and skip the verifier. This is true of EVERY shipped work class; it is the existing threat boundary (host secret trusted), and the relay class is strictly stronger than what ships while NOT moving that boundary. Claim exactly that and nothing more. Any claim of byzantine-fault tolerance from this soak is to be REFUTED.

STANDING LAYERING LAW + a verified gap. The relay node-agent is L1 BY DEFINITION (olamnit PC + gavri PC as hosts; tablet + phone as MAUI) — the same byte-exact source must run in both worlds. But L1 DOES NOT EXIST YET (Olamnit.Shared -> Olamnit.Kernel = 0 references; the MAUI and host worlds are disjoint), and the rewards project is anchored in the MAUI world by its imports. Therefore: do NOT fork the adapter/corroborator per world (forbidden peers). Put the E-A/E-B logic behind an L0 contract with an L1-shaped core, and keep host-specific couplings (durable-store handles) at the L3/L4 seam (the IFormFactor pattern). If L1 genuinely cannot be reached this iteration, ESCALATE it — do not quietly duplicate.

The coin leg adds EXACTLY ONE new adapter (a relay-transmit work-signal adapter) over the SHIPPED rewards engine, plus the E-B corroborator (registration-only into the existing DI enumerable). Minter, wallet, identity, endorsement, epoch and provenance are reused VERBATIM. Scope discipline: 1 ucoin per ACKED hop to the successor; 1 coin = 1,000,000 ucoin; 1M hops ~ 1 coin/node; 4 wallets replicated per node, surviving kill-one. Any design requiring a second new adapter or a fork of the rewards engine is out of scope and must be ESCALATED, not absorbed.

The @mesh service's runtime DI resolve is NULL today, so it answers Unavailable. Closing this is a precondition for M-03. INVESTIGATE: what must change to make it real WITHOUT violating wrap-never-replace (FR-010)? Is there a design where the relay rides the mailbox spine end-to-end and still satisfies the operator's intent? A proposal that replaces rather than wraps is to be rejected.

HONESTY GATE — answer plainly, even if the answer is unwelcome. A logical relay order pins a sequence; DV routing chooses next-hops. Does the relay ordering BYPASS the routing layer, and if so what does a 1M-cycle soak actually prove about the mesh (liveness? framing? exactly-once? or ONLY the crypto chain)? If it proves less than the operator expects, SAY SO — that finding is wanted now, not after the run. Also adjudicate the split proposal (1M all-WiFi + 10k heterogeneous with a BLE leg) against the requirement '>=1,000,000 cycles over a BT+WiFi mesh': is it honest, or a dodge? Recorded input: BLE L2CAP RTT p50 = 122 ms (feature 013, 2-node, measured).

NO ASSERT-WITHOUT-VERIFY. Every claim must rest on a file:line, a committed record, or a measured number, named in the claim. This method was authored after two recorded failures of exactly this kind on this feature: a peer's critic INFERRED a branch state from a local checkout and passed it through unverified (refuted by fetched remote refs), and the lead carried a wrong premise about a symbol's existence. Both were caught only by cross-checking. A claim resting on inference from an adjacent fact must be marked as such or dropped. Prefer 'I could not verify X' over a confident wrong X.

A concurrent automation drives the lead's primary clone and is mid-refactor, relocating mesh routing sources between projects on an uncommitted branch. It has ALREADY caused one test to silently run the wrong code. Therefore every read and every live test for this run executes in an ISOLATED git worktree pinned to a named commit — never the shared working tree. Evidence citing a path must be reproducible at that pinned commit. If a cited path does not exist at the pin, the claim is void.
